Great! Let me help you work through the Child Benefit eligibility assessment. I need to ask you some questions to determine your eligibility.

First, I need to know about the child or children you're asking about:

**How old is your child (or children)?** 

This is important because:
- Children under 16 generally qualify automatically
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children aged 20 or over don't qualify for Child Benefit

Please tell me the age(s) of the child/children you're inquiring about.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! Based on the assessment, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why you qualify:

✅ **Alex is 8 years old** - Under 16, so qualifies as a "qualifying young person"
✅ **Alex is not working full-time** - Not working 24+ hours per week
✅ **Alex is not receiving benefits** - Not receiving benefits in their own right
✅ **Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship**
✅ **You meet UK residency requirements** - You normally live in the UK
✅ **You are responsible for Alex** - You're contributing £30.00 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which meets the requirement (the minimum is £26.05/week currently)
✅ **No one else is claiming** - No one who lives with Alex is already claiming Child Benefit
✅ **Alex's location is standard** - Not in local authority care, hospital, or foster care
✅ **Council not paying** - The local council is not paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance

**Important note about your situation:** You mentioned you are adopting Alex but Alex has not yet come to live with you. This is actually covered under the "contributing to upkeep" pathway - as long as you're contributing at least the Child Benefit amount towards Alex's care (which you are), you can claim.

**Next Steps:**

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide documentation** - such as Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you'll need to pay back some or all of the benefit through the tax system
5. **Payments** will be made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

You can apply at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
